interpretation.summary: Frequency-dependent apparent sources predict 131.6 dB over 13 one-third-octave bands at (-25, 0, 20) m. The same reference geometry gives 131.6 dB before incremental water treatment.
interpretation.physicalMeaning: Changing engine power changes generated acoustic watts. Nozzle size and velocity set spectral similarity; source locations and deflector turning change each propagation distance and radiation angle. This result is external pressure in the incident free field, not structural vibration or internal noise.
engineeringConsiderations: A deflector may lower total power and raise loading at this receiver through geometry/directivity. Compare the same reference before assigning attenuation.
Each dB reduction is applied to its named stage once; water flow has no universal noise-reduction law.
Retain source provenance and missing tails when transferring this spectrum into a structural or SEA model.

satisfied: Canonical SI internally; sound power referenced to 1 pW, pressure to 20 µPa.

limitations: Empirical handbook similarity and coarse digitization are not engine/pad measurement correlation or qualification.
Ignition overpressure, shock tones, multiphase water dynamics, coherent reflections, structural vibration and internal response require separate models.
